title: Protecting America's Food and Agriculture Act of 2019
official_summary:
Protecting America's Food and Agriculture Act of 2019

This bill authorizes U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), every fiscal year, to hire, train, and assign 240 new agricultural specialists until the total number of specialists equals and sustains the requirements identified each year in the Agriculture Resource Allocation Model.

The CBP may also hire, train, and assign support staff to assist the specialists and specified levels of agricultural canine teams.

In calculating the number of specialists needed at each port of entry through the Agriculture Resource Allocation Model, the Office of Field Operations of the CBP must (1) rely on data collected regarding the inspections and other activities conducted at each such port of entry; and (2) consider volume from seasonal surges, other projected changes in commercial and passenger volumes, the most current commercial forecasts, and other relevant information.

The Government Accountability Office (GAO) must conduct a review of the efforts of the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Agriculture, and other federal agencies to address risks to the agricultural supply. The GAO must analyze (1) interagency coordination and the distribution of responsibilities among federal agencies with respect to the inspection of agricultural commodities entering the United States; (2) the effectiveness of such inspection responsibilities among federal agencies; and (3) the training provided to, and working conditions of, CBP Agriculture Specialists.

summary.headline: This law lets Customs and Border Protection hire 240 new agricultural specialists each year and orders a federal review of how farm and food imports are inspected.
summary.what_it_does: The law authorizes U.S. Customs and Border Protection to hire, train, and assign 240 new agricultural specialists each fiscal year until staffing matches the number set by an annual staffing model. It also allows the agency to add support staff and certain agricultural detector dog teams. The staffing model counts inspection data, seasonal surges, and trade and travel forecasts at each port of entry. The Government Accountability Office must review how federal agencies coordinate and carry out inspections of farm products entering the country, including specialist training and working conditions.

who_it_affects.how: The law authorizes the agency to hire and train new specialists and requires a review of their training and working conditions.

who_it_affects.group: Importers and shippers of agricultural goods
who_it_affects.how: Staffing at ports of entry may increase over time, which could change how quickly farm and food shipments are inspected.

who_it_affects.group: Travelers arriving at U.S. ports of entry
who_it_affects.how: Added agricultural staff and detector dog teams may change how luggage and passengers are screened for farm items.
The law targets inspection of agricultural commodities entering the country to address risks to the domestic food and farm supply.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The hiring authority applies each fiscal year starting with the law's enactment on March 3, 2020, and the GAO review is required after enactment, with no specific deadline stated in the summary.
